certificate: URT icosahedral shell conditional uniqueness theorem

exact_conference_classification.graph_consequence: the +1 graph on five vertices is 2-regular, hence C5; there is one switching/permutation class
exact_conference_classification.row_sum_consequence: (S^2)_1j=0 forces two +1 and two -1 entries in every row of the remaining 5x5 block
exact_conference_classification.switching_normalization: sign-switch axes so S_1j=+1 for j>1

exact_projective_design_proof.frame_operator: sum_i u_i tensor u_i=(4/5) I_5 from the fourth moment
exact_projective_design_proof.zero_sum: sum_i u_i=0 from the second moment

icosahedron_consequence.statement: The six axes are unique up to O(3), sign switching and permutation. Their twelve signed endpoints are the regular icosahedron.
icosahedron_consequence.status: E conditional on the stated moment/antipodality premises
icosahedron_consequence.valence: For each vertex, exactly one endpoint on each of the other five axes has inner product +1/sqrt(5), so the nearest-neighbour degree is 5.

premises.directions: 12 unit vectors in R^3 grouped as six antipodal pairs +/-v_i
premises.fourth_moment: sum over 12 directions n_a^{tensor 4}=(4/5)(delta_ij delta_kl+delta_ik delta_jl+delta_il delta_jk)
premises.second_moment: sum over 12 directions n_a tensor n_a = 4 I_3
premises.weights: equal nonzero weight on the 12 moving directions plus one rest state

verdict.closed: No other 12-direction antipodal equal-weight shell satisfies the stated exact second/fourth isotropy up to rotation.
verdict.remaining_premise: Derive, rather than postulate, why the microscopic action requires antipodality and exact second/fourth isotropy with six axes.
